lines: A friend of the courier's sent us. You have tasted the sap. You are hurt.
The boat takes the hurt to a house in Lilmoth. That includes you.
A friend of the courier's sent us. You are hurt, as the others here are hurt. The boat takes the hurt to a house in Lilmoth.
The shed stands beside the withdrawn cutting, at the camp's far end. Sap lies spilled on its floor.

The burnt boards lie over deep water at the camp's fire. The courier's strap and tag lie in the gang families' locked fish-trap on the bottom, straight below them. Lockpicks lie loose beside the fire.

I watched from the shore at the end of my shift. A woman with a knotted cord at her wrist led the cell. She took the courier's satchel. She left the cutting to her cutters. The roots were cut clean at the ring, one stroke each, by hands that knew where.
Wuleen-Sei marched the unhurt back to the barge at the dock, because hurt hands are no hire.

lines: I saw the camp that night. I do not tell strangers what I saw. Give me a reason.
I am of the Veiled Reed. It is the state's quiet service. We show no face. We want a hand we can deny.
No master can claim you now. The roll burnt in the camp's fire, so the broker cannot show what you owe, or that you were ever on it.
I offer you the Reed's protection, a door in Lilmoth and a stipend. The condition is that you serve the Reed. Think before you answer.
I want the survivor's account of the cell's work. When I have it, the Reed's people see the survivor home.
Then you serve the Reed. The protection, the door in Lilmoth and the stipend are yours now. I have your word.
Then you do not take the Reed's protection, the door in Lilmoth or the stipend. That is your choice. The Reed will still send for you, and it will pay for the work.
